literal: Of what use will a long-standing friendship be, if one does not accept when a friend acts with intimate freedom accordingly?
translation: Of what use is a long-standing friendship if one cannot graciously accept and accommodate a friend's actions done with the freedom of intimacy?
modern: நண்பர்கள் உரிமை எடுத்துக்கொண்டு செய்யும் செயல்களை அப்படியே ஏற்றுக்கொண்டு உடன்படாதபோது, பழமையான நட்பினால் என்ன பயன் விளையும்?
explanation: This couplet defines the core of long-standing friendship, which is the right to act with intimate freedom (keḻutakaimai) without fear of offending. If a person cannot happily accept and accommodate their friend's actions when they take such liberties, the long-standing friendship loses its value. The word 'keḻutakaimai' denotes the privilege of intimacy where formal permission is unnecessary. True friendship is proven not by mere duration, but by the capacity to tolerate and welcome the free, unconstrained actions of a close friend.
